comparator.name: Wiskunde (Mathematics)
comparator.sourceNotes: The ordinary Mathematics pathway closes 60+60+60 with 82.5 EC compulsory study, one selected 7.5-EC modelling course, 15 EC restricted choice, 30 EC further mathematics choice and 45 EC genuine profiling. The selected set meets the 30-EC major level-3 minimum. Modelling preparation is treated as advisory rather than invented as a hard prerequisite. Mathematics and Applications is not substituted. Formal instruction is Dutch plus English.

alternatives.label: Applied mathematics, algorithms & stochastic data models
alternatives.concept: Develop calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability and linear systems through programming, logic, algorithms, optimisation, statistical learning and empirical stochastic models. This is the strongest applied and computational response to the stated Mathematics interests; proof-intensive analysis, algebra, geometry, topology and mathematical research remain explicit gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum contains a sustained mathematical and computational spine with concrete algorithmic and stochastic applications, while the label avoids claiming the target programme’s proof-intensive pure-mathematics depth.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in year one and nine advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Programming precedes algorithms and autonomous decisions; Mathematical Methods precedes dependent mathematics, robotics and neural networks. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Econometrics, while Probability & Statistics and Statistics & Experimental Methods precede the final empirical modelling work.

alternatives.label: Mathematical modelling, Earth systems & scientific data
alternatives.concept: Use calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability, differential and linear-system models, programming and scientific data analysis to study Earth systems, climate, water–mineral processes, resources and renewable-energy systems. This answers the explicit mathematics-for-climate direction without presenting Earth science as full Mathematics equivalence.
alternatives.labelReason: Thirteen mathematical/computational courses form the method spine, while ten Earth, climate, resource and energy courses supply coherent scientific systems to model and analyse.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in year one and eight advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and all dependent resource courses. Mathematical Methods precedes later mathematics, robotics and neural-network courses. Environmental foundations precede advanced biogeochemistry, recovery, resources and energy work.
alternatives.distinctness: Ten courses / 75 EC differ from the closest programme. The Earth-systems route replaces economics, general research methods, optimisation, networks, advanced algorithms, human-data statistics, decision-making and reinforcement learning with sustainability foundations, Earth-system analysis, field/laboratory environmental science, climate, resources and energy technology.

alternatives.label: Mathematics, economics & quantitative decision models
alternatives.concept: Apply calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability, statistics, optimisation and data modelling to economics, corporate finance, strategic interaction, public policy and econometrics. This responds to the explicit mathematics-for-economics and financial-mathematics directions while preserving the absence of a dedicated financial-mathematics or proof-intensive pure-mathematics sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum retains a substantial mathematics, statistics, computation and optimisation spine while adding finance, macroeconomics, microeconomics, public economics and econometrics, so the label names mathematics, economics and quantitative decision models together.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in Year 1 and seven advanced courses. Programming, economics and corporate-finance foundations begin in Semester 1. Mathematical Methods and Research Methods precede linear algebra, probability, econometrics and advanced quantitative work; Algorithms & Data Structures precedes Advanced Algorithms. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026 cohort semester.
alternatives.distinctness: Against the applied computational route, five courses / 37.5 EC in each direction change: networks, image processing, linear systems, robotics and deep learning are replaced by accounting and corporate finance, ethics, public economics, international macroeconomics and advanced microeconomics. Against the Earth-systems route, fourteen courses / 105 EC differ in each direction. These changes follow from making economic and financial decision models, rather than technological or Earth systems, the application centre.

selection.assessment: Three complete related-fields programmes pass the evidence, coherence, course-content, pairwise distinctness and feasibility gates. The closest route integrates mathematical methods with algorithms, optimisation, probability and data models. The second uses the explicit climate direction to organise a materially different Earth-system and scientific-data curriculum. The third uses the explicit mathematics-for-economics and financial-mathematics interests to organise a quantitative economics and decision-model route. All pairwise differences exceed 30 EC. The biological/life-science and history-of-mathematics directions remain recorded but are not pursued beyond the maximum of three. None of the accepted curricula is presented as proof-intensive pure Mathematics.

blocks: Both provide programming for mathematical problem solving; UCR supplies a general Python foundation rather than mathematics-specific research programming.
Both develop discrete mathematical reasoning; UCR emphasises logic, discrete structures and algorithm construction.
Both establish calculus and linear-algebra techniques; UCR combines these with complex numbers and differential equations.
Both develop matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations; the external component also continues calculus.
Both model systems with differential equations; UCR concentrates on linear systems, transforms and state-space representations rather than the full ODE/PDE modelling course.
Both establish probability; UCR integrates probability distributions with estimation, inference and simulation.
Both develop multivariable analysis; UCR combines it with complex functions and differential equations and does not reproduce the external proof-intensive sequence.
Both use formal strategic interaction and game-theoretic reasoning; UCR embeds it in advanced microeconomics and behavioural economics.
UCR logic courses develop formal reasoning, but no selected course reproduces a dedicated proof-writing foundation.
UCR calculus does not reproduce a cumulative proof-intensive analysis course.
UCR has no abstract algebra course in groups and rings.
UCR Advanced Calculus is already aligned with the later multivariable-analysis component; this separate introductory progression remains visible.
UCR Advanced Calculus includes complex functions but does not reproduce a dedicated complex-analysis course.
General projects and research methods do not reproduce the target’s dedicated mathematics laboratory.
The genuine 15-EC profiling space remains open and is not assigned invented UCR course identities.
No scheduled UCR course is represented as the target’s 15-EC mathematics bachelor thesis; optional independent research is comparison-only.
The genuine 30-EC profiling space remains open and is not assigned invented UCR course identities.

notes.text: The UCR pathways provide substantial calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, differential and linear-system models, probability, programming, optimisation and data analysis. They do not reproduce Utrecht Mathematics’ cumulative proof-intensive analysis, abstract algebra, topology, complex analysis, differentiable manifolds, mathematics laboratory or dedicated mathematics thesis formation.
